text:
maria: quick FYI — found ~15 KMS-wrapped objects in partner-logs-bucket that reference an old service-account (svc-archive@redwood-prod). We rotated that SA last week, but these ciphertexts could be unwrapped by anyone with the old key. unclear if these are exfil or leftover backups. starting a containment thread.

alex: do we have object names? can you paste a short sample path and the KMS key resource?

maria: example: gs://partner-logs-bucket/2025-11-03/export/enc_blob_20251103.gz.enc -> kmsKeyName: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/partner/cryptoKeys/partner-wrap/cryptoKeyVersions/3

jen: ack. if the key version 3 is still ENABLED we should consider disabling it until we validate. but disabling will break any team still using it for legit unwraps.

defon: +1 on quick audit. steps I'd propose: 1) list principals with decrypt on that cryptoKey, 2) snapshot the ciphertexts (for forensics), 3) temporarily remove decrypt binding from the SA and partner service accounts, 4) consult partner legal/ops before mass rotate.

alex: to list IAM bindings quickly:
```
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy partner-wrap --location global --keyring partner --project redwood
```
I'll run that now and paste results.

sre-bot: deploy-status: nightly-data-export job 2025-11-03 completed (job-id: ne-20251103-48). No immediate failures.

alex: IAM shows: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter bound to serviceAccount:svc-archive@redwood-prod, and to group:partner-ingest@partners.redwood.com.

maria: ok that matches the worry. I want the SA removed first (we rotated keys for it). jen can you remove the decrypt role from svc-archive and hold on revoking partner group until we confirm scope? do it with an audit log entry so we can trace.

jen: removing now. command: 
```
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding partner-wrap \
  --location global --keyring partner --member serviceAccount:svc-archive@redwood-prod \
  --role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
Will also add a retention note in the audit ticket.

oncall-bot: Incident channel created: #inc-6789-credential-containment. Pager duty alerted: security-oncall.

devon: while jen runs that, I'll snapshot the 15 objects to a locked-forensics bucket (read-only for security+legal). command I'm using:
```
gsutil cp gs://partner-logs-bucket/2025-11-03/export/enc_blob_20251103.gz.enc gs://sec-forensic-snapshots/6789012345/
```

maria: perfect. once SA binding is removed and snapshots done, we need to decide: 1) rotate the cryptoKey (create new primary version and revoke old), 2) run a targeted key rewrap for active backups, or 3) ask partner to rotate client-side keys if they used their own. my preference is minimal blast radius: rotate key (create v4), set v3 to disabled, and do rewrap for any objects we know are legit.

alex: rewrapping at scale is noisy. recommend we: create v4, update partner export job to use v4, and run rewrap only for objects with last-access < 7d? risk-based.

jen: legal says if partner data may have been exfiltrated we have to notify them per contract. I've pinged partner-ops.

maria: action items: jen -> remove SA binding & add audit entry (in progress), devon -> snapshot objects + upload to sec-forensic-snapshots (in progress), alex -> prepare key v4 creation and doc the rewrap plan, I'll coordinate partner notification and escalate to legal if partner confirms suspected access. tagging security-oncall to lead the postmortem and timeline collection.

alex: I'll also enable more verbose audit logging for Cloud KMS and GCS access for the partner key for the next 30 days. commands:
```
# enable audit logging (conceptual)
gcloud logging sinks create kms-access-sink ...
```

maria: thanks team. keep updates in #inc-6789-credential-containment and post here when we have v4 and the binding removal timestamp. :thumbsup:
